title: Validator‑Guided Repair on a Shared Initial LLM Candidate: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation for Network Configuration Safety
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) to measure whether a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline changes the executability of LLM‑produced network configurations when the same single sampled candidate per intent is deterministically reused across baseline and guarded arms (shared_initial_candidate semantics). The experiment used gpt‑5‑mini (declared) to produce exactly one initial generation per intent which was deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded episodes; a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) produced binary valid/invalid labels and the guarded arm permitted one automated repair if violations were detected. Confirmatory execution (task_count = 200 pairs; completed_episode_count = 400; model_calls_used = 200) produced baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100% each). Paired contingency: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0]. No repairs were applied because every shared initial candidate was validator‑valid. We document preregistration, execution accounting, representative validator traces, and a calibrated interpretation of the null paired effect constrained by shared_initial_candidate semantics and an archived model configuration field temperature = null (unset). We close with concrete, artifact‑grounded recommendations for follow‑on confirmatory designs that would change the estimand to test repair efficacy under sampling variability.

sections.introduction:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly investigated for intent→configuration workflows in network operations (NetOps). Hallucination, syntactic errors, and logic faults in generated device configurations pose operational safety risks when outputs are executed. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipelines—where generation is followed by a deterministic validator and optional automated repair—are a plausible mitigation strategy, but the empirical effect of such pipelines depends on experimental semantics (for example, whether each experimental arm receives independent model samples). We preregistered the narrowly scoped confirmatory question: does applying a deterministic validator plus one automated repair to a fixed single LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics) change the rate of validator‑valid, executable configurations relative to reusing the same candidate without validation/repair? The primary estimand was the paired difference in executable success rate (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) under paired, shared_initial_candidate execution.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) executed with deterministic artifact capture and reproducible analysis; (2) an artifact‑grounded evaluation on 200 paired intents using gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with exact per‑condition accounting; (3) a transparent interpretation of a degenerate null paired effect that arises from shared_initial_candidate sampling semantics, and concrete recommendations for follow‑on preregistered designs that change the estimand to measure repair efficacy under sampling variability.
sections.related_work: Prior literature documents LLM reliability problems (hallucination and reference unreliability) across domains and motivates evidence‑grounded generation and post‑generation verification [1,2]. In operations‑style QA and documentation tasks, retrieval‑ or evidence‑grounded approaches reduce hallucination rates relative to naive generation in the supplied evaluations [2]. Tool‑assisted GVR architectures and verifier‑guided feedback loops have been shown to improve correctness in infrastructure‑as‑code and program‑generation contexts (TerraFormer and related verifier‑guided fine‑tuning/repair proposals), though those demonstrations are typically outside device‑level NetOps execution studies [3]. NetOps LLM evaluations in the supplied corpus measure translation and capability but generally do not provide standardized execution‑level safety measurements in packet‑level simulators or paired estimator semantics [4]. These prior findings motivated the preregistered paired experiment: to produce machine‑verifiable artifacts and a deterministic validator trace suitable for a narrowly specified estimand.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01. The primary estimand was the per‑intent paired difference in proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations between guarded and baseline (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The preregistration fixed a paired design with task_count = 200 and generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; it also fixed the maximum permitted repair attempts per task to 1 and specified exact analysis tests (McNemar exact two‑sided) plus a paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). The preregistration document (preregistration_sha256 = f0c8330d3d74cb95461d3f0291ba1b607c427ad37b5edc3750cad593bd4aae76) is archived with the evidence bundle.

Task bank, selection, and contamination checks. A deterministic task generator produced a fixed task manifest of N = 200 synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' intents; task selection was fixed prior to any model calls per the sampling_plan. Each manifest entry records an initial_state, required_sequence, difficulty annotation, and generation_seed for reproducibility (representative entries include generation_seed values such as 4, 5, 6 in the archived task_manifest). Preregistered contamination detection (SHA256 exact‑match and high‑similarity n‑gram thresholds) ran prior to execution and flagged no exact‑match exclusions; the analysis/contamination_summary.csv in the archive is empty (no flagged items).

Generation semantics and model configuration. Execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded episodes. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini via hosted adapter openai_responses; model configuration is archived at execution/model_configuration.json (sha256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). That file records temperature = null (unset); per preregistration and the methods specification we report null/unset explicitly and note that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Provider audit. Provider audit metadata recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_miss_count = 200, and a single stage count labeled shared_initial_generation = 200 (deterministic_reconciliation provider_call_audit). The adapter enforced planned maximum_model_calls = 400 but model_calls_used = 200 because one shared initial generation per pair was produced and reused.

Validator and repair pipeline. Scoring employed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_version = 5.0) using the scoring_rule 'full_intent_constraint_validation' to map generated candidates to a binary valid/invalid executable label. For guarded episodes the pipeline was allowed a single automated repair attempt if the validator flagged violations (preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Shared_initial_candidate semantics mean that the same initial candidate could only be altered by validator‑triggered repair on the guarded side; the baseline reused the same candidate without repair.

Analysis plan. The primary test was an exact two‑sided McNemar test on the paired 2×2 contingency table; primary analysis used the complete_pair_primary policy (exclude incomplete pairs). We report exact p‑values and the paired absolute risk difference with 95% paired bootstrap percentile CIs (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). Exploratory failure‑category distributions and subgroup analyses were declared exploratory and planned for Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction at 0.05 if discordant pairs appeared. All analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv) are archived with their SHA256 hashes.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter executed the preregistered plan: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (execution_manifest fields). No episodes were omitted, failed, or unscorable according to the archived missingness summary (complete_pairs = 200; failed_baseline_episodes = 0; failed_guarded_episodes = 0).

Primary outcomes. Baseline_success_count = 200/200 (100%), guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100%); success_rate_baseline = 1.0; success_rate_guarded = 1.0. Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided test: p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) paired percentile 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0]. These numeric results and their analysis files are archived under analysis/ with provided SHA256 hashes (e.g., analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c).

Repair activity and validator traces. Zero repair prompts were issued in the guarded arm because every shared initial candidate passed validator checks: repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 (these counts are present in the per‑episode scoring artifacts; representative episode JSONs show validator.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false). Representative artifacts include task‑000004, task‑000005, and task‑000006 scoring JSONs archived under execution/scoring (example SHA256s: task-000004-baseline.json sha256 = 46847f21..., task-000004-guarded.json sha256 = 40831812...); these files contain shared_initial_candidate text, normalized_configuration, and validator.trace entries demonstrating validator.valid = true and identical final_configuration for baseline and guarded.

Missingness, contamination, and reconciliation. All preregistered contamination checks passed (analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged items). Deterministic reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent episode accounting; all deterministic consistency checks passed (deterministic_reconciliation.json archived). The provider_call_audit shows cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false, consistent with the declared shared_initial_generation stage semantics rather than cross‑condition sampling differences.

Statistical interpretation. The observed degenerate contingency table (zero discordant pairs) produces an exact McNemar p = 1.0 and a bootstrap CI of [0.0,0.0]: these inferential values faithfully reflect the executed estimand and observed outcomes but are uninformative about potential repair efficacy under alternative sampling regimes. In other words, within the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics there were no validator‑detectable faults for the sampled candidates and therefore no opportunity for repair to affect the paired outcome.
sections.discussion:
Causal interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate design intentionally isolates downstream validator/repair effects on a fixed sampled candidate. Because the single shared initial candidate per intent was valid under deterministic_netops_validator_v5 for all 200 tasks, the guarded pipeline could not alter any outcome and the paired difference is therefore exactly zero. This is a narrow, evidence‑grounded scientific conclusion about the executed estimand only; it does not imply that (a) GVR pipelines are unnecessary more broadly, (b) other models or prompt strategies would always produce valid candidates, or (c) repairs would not help under adversarial or higher‑difficulty sampling.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics and reuse of a single sampled candidate per pair restrict internal inference to validator/repair effects on that same candidate and preclude any sampling‑driven differences. Execution accounting shows model_calls_used = 200 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200}, confirming this sampling policy. Construct validity: the deterministic validator abstracts device behavior and enforces the preregistered scoring_rule; vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, timing, or dynamic runtime interactions were not executed on live devices. External validity: a single declared model/provider (gpt‑5‑mini via openai_responses), synthetic task bank, and validator abstraction limit generalizability to diverse production NetOps contexts. Conclusion validity: the degenerate zero‑discordant outcome provides no basis to estimate repair efficacy under sampling variability; larger or different‑semantics confirmatory designs are required to observe discordant pairs and credibly test hypotheses about repair impact.

Operational implications and recommendations. The run establishes a fully artifacted GVR evaluation pipeline (preregistration, provider audit, deterministic validator traces, and reproducible analysis) that can be reconfigured to measure alternative estimands. To test repair efficacy under realistic sampling variability we recommend preregistered follow‑on designs that (1) produce independent per‑condition first‑pass samples (i.e., do not reuse the same candidate across arms), (2) introduce adversarial or intentionally higher‑difficulty task subsets to increase expected discordant pair counts, (3) vary temperature or sampling settings explicitly and record them (avoid temperature=null/unset ambiguity), (4) include multiple model families/providers, and (5) increase validator fidelity (vendor CLI specifics or packet‑level emulation) so repairs can be evaluated against dynamic runtime behavior. Each recommendation changes the estimand and must be preregistered accordingly.

Representative diagnostics and why the archive matters. The archived per‑task JSONs (execution/scoring/task‑000004‑baseline.json, task‑000004‑guarded.json, etc.) demonstrate that identical shared_initial_candidate SHA256s and identical validator.validation_after.normalized_configuration values occurred in both conditions for representative hard tasks. The analysis artifacts and deterministic_reconciliation.json provide machine‑verifiable accounting that supports the manuscript claims. We include these representative examples here to make explicit the artifact grounding of the reported degenerate pathway and to satisfy reviewers' requests for repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 as immediate diagnostics.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measured the downstream effect of deterministic validation and a single permitted automated repair on a fixed LLM‑generated candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Under these execution semantics and with the archived configuration (gpt‑5‑mini; model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset), every shared initial candidate passed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and no repairs were applied; therefore guarded and baseline conditions were identical on the executed estimand (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap CI = [0.0,0.0]). The study contributes a reproducible, artifacted evaluation pipeline and clarifies that experimental sampling semantics (shared initial candidate versus independent per‑condition sampling) crucially determine what a confirmatory paired experiment can, and cannot, show. Follow‑on preregistered experiments that change sampling semantics, increase task difficulty, diversify models, and raise validator fidelity are required to evaluate whether GVR pipelines reduce executable misconfiguration rates under realistic sampling variability.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single sampled initial generation was reused across baseline and guarded conditions; this design measures validator/repair effects only and cannot detect differences caused by independent per‑condition sampling or prompt engineering.

Temperature unset (temperature = null) in execution/model_configuration.json: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still have occurred during the single sampled generation.
Single model and single hosted provider: results reflect gpt‑5‑mini under the archived adapter; generalization to other models or model families is unsupported by these artifacts.

Synthetic task bank and validator abstraction: tasks were synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' items and the deterministic validator is an abstraction; realistic vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, emergent runtime interactions, and hardware effects were not executed on live devices.

No observed validator failures: all initial candidates were validator‑valid, so the experiment could not assess the repair step's effectiveness; the null effect therefore reflects the task bank and sampling semantics rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.
